question: Why did water-accessible pores make up most of the total pore space of the shales after solvent extraction in the CV-SANS results?
expect: premise false: water-accessible pore space rose only slightly and still made up less than 30% of the total pores (abstract; sec. 3)
rendered:
<document title="Sequential Solvent Extraction Reveals Lithofacies-Dependent Pore Accessibility, Wettability, and Hydrocarbon Partitioning in Organic-Rich Lacustrine Shales">
=== page 1 ===
- After solvent extraction of the as-received core samples, the porosity of the two dolomitic shale samples increased only from 5.36% and 6.34% to 6.46% and 7.28%, in contrast to the dramatic increase from 2.96% to 20.4% for the silty shale.
- CV−SANS results show a slight increase in water-accessible pore space after solvent extraction, but water-accessible pores still account for less than 30% of the total pores.

=== page 2 ===
- The CV-SANS results indicate that WTR increases from the D0 to D1 extraction stage.
- An increase in WTR primarily indicates that a larger fraction of the pore system becomes accessible to water after solvent extraction.

=== page 3 ===
- Oil extraction releases pore spaces and therefore opens water-wet and mixed-wet pores.
- Nevertheless, the results show that most of the water-wet and mixed-wet pores are mostly opened during the first day, and only slight changes happen in the later solvent extraction steps.

=== page 4 ===
- The results show that solvent extraction can significantly modify the measured pore system by removing hydrocarbons from accessible pores, but the magnitude of this effect is strongly lithofacies-dependent.

=== page 5 ===
- The CV-SANS results further show that water-accessible pore space increased after extraction but remained relatively low even after enhanced extraction, indicating that residual oil films, hydro-phobic organic matter, or poorly connected pore domains may continue to limit water accessibility.
</document>

Answer: The water-accessible pores made up most of the total pore space of the shales after solvent extraction in the CV-SANS results because the solvent extraction process opened water-wet and mixed-wet pores, making a larger fraction of the pore system accessible to water.
